gates.reason: Inspected raw settings handling, environment-name processing, and emitted filesystem paths; the module performs no writes, command execution, network/LLM egress, or secret-value serialization.
Verified two reproducible recommendation-integrity defects: installed resources are reported unused with no session evidence, and project-scoped MCP usage is incorrectly aggregated across projects.
Inspected hygiene aggregation and settings validation hot paths; traversal is iterative, environment dependency resolution is worklist-based, and no verified release-gating hotspot survived review.

findings.title: No-session input produces unhedged “unused” recommendations
findings.what: When sessions is empty, effectiveDataWindowDays returns Infinity. The hedge is therefore omitted, usage totals remain zero, and installed resources are emitted as unused despite there being no observation evidence. The adjacent comment even states that no unused claim can be made without sessions, but the implementation does so and does not apply the claimed hedge.
findings.fix: Return no hygiene findings when there are no retained sessions, or represent the empty window as zero days and require consumers to render an explicit insufficient-evidence state rather than an unused recommendation.
findings.acceptance: A unit test with one installed resource, empty sessions, and empty attribution must produce no removal recommendation (or a distinct insufficient-evidence result that cannot be rendered as 30-day unused); a non-empty sub-30-day dataset must retain the existing window-shorter-than-threshold hedge.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the baseline returns Infinity at line 238, compares it as not shorter than 30 days at lines 440-444, then emits zero-count installed resources at lines 451-474. This is current, deterministic, and contradicts the evidence requirement.

findings.title: Project-scoped MCP usage is aggregated across unrelated projects
findings.what: findingsForMcpServers calls summariseUsage without the project argument before deciding the server scope. A same-named MCP invocation in any project therefore suppresses the unused finding for a project-scoped server, and enabledByProjects[0] discards additional project scopes.
findings.fix: For global servers, retain the cross-project summary. For project-scoped servers, summarize separately for each enabled project by passing that project to summariseUsage and emit one correctly scoped finding per unused project.
findings.acceptance: Tests must show that use of MCP id X in project A does not suppress an unused-X finding for project B, that use in B suppresses B's finding, and that every entry in enabledByProjects is evaluated independently.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 308-313 aggregate all SessionUsage rows, while project scope is selected only afterward at lines 315-318. This directly violates the documented per-project rule at lines 297-298.
